recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. Any desired convenience search directly on Practitioner for related PractitionerRole role/specialty should be raised as a new current-model search-design issue, not treated as remaining FHIR-5269 application work.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive DSTU1 Practitioner ballot comment #148 requested adding Specialty and Role search parameters because those were expected to be commonly desired Practitioner searches.
initial_application: Historical commit 8ed9982708ac31ba37ad6670f9be8ba628634329 listed tracker 5269 in a Practitioner ballot reconciliation batch and added role and specialty token search rows to the then-current Practitioner spreadsheet over Practitioner.practitionerRole.role and Practitioner.practitionerRole.specialty.
additional_context: The latest combined branch actively builds both Practitioner and PractitionerRole. The old nested Practitioner.practitionerRole structure has since become the separate PractitionerRole resource. Current PractitionerRole defines code and specialty elements and exposes role and specialty token search parameters; current Practitioner does not define role or specialty properties. Later Published R5 decisions FHIR-25033 and FHIR-32497 clarify that PractitionerRole.specialty is role-specific and distinct from general Practitioner qualifications.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Adding direct Practitioner role/specialty search parameters would not match the current resource model; the requested searchable concepts already exist on PractitionerRole and can be connected to Practitioner through PractitionerRole.practitioner.

related_jiras.note: Later Published decision clarifies PractitionerRole.specialty as the role-specific concept and says such specialties are not defined on Practitioner. Already represented on the combined branch.
Later Published decision reinforces that PractitionerRole.specialty is role-specific and distinct from general Practitioner qualifications. Already represented on the combined branch.
